title: Isolation and Decellularization of a Whole Porcine Pancreas
protocol: Prepare the decellularization set-up using 3 x 5 mm silicone tubes.
Connect the detergent inlet container to the peristaltic pump.
Connect the peristaltic pump to the degasser.
Connect the degasser to the pancreas in the organ chamber.
Attach a male luer to the free end of the tube in the organ chamber.
Use another 3 x 5 mm silicone tube to connect the organ chamber to the detergent outlet container.
Connect the outlet container via the peristaltic pump.
Collect perfused detergent from the organ chamber into the outlet container.
Attach a 2 ml unlabeled pipette to the free ends of tubes in both containers.
Maintain the entire set-up at 4 °C.
Add 8 g of sodium chloride, 0.2 g of potassium chloride, 1.44 g of sodium phosphate, and 0.24 g of potassium phosphate to 1 L of ultrapure water.
Stir until dissolved.
Adjust the pH to 7.4 with hydrochloric acid (HCl).
Prepare 3.2 L of this solution for Solution 1.
Add 3.4 mL of heparin (17 IU/mL) to 1 L of Solution 1.
Keep this solution on ice until it becomes cold.
Prepare a total volume of 1.2 L of this solution for Solution 2.
Add 1.86 g of EDTA and 200 mg of sodium azide to 1 L of ultrapure water.
Stir until the salts are dissolved.
Cool the solution to 4 °C before use.
Prepare a total volume of 22 L of this solution for Solution 3.
Add 200 mg of sodium azide and 1.86 g of EDTA to 1 L of Solution 1.
Stir until the salts are dissolved.
Cool the solution to 4 °C before use.
Prepare a total volume of 1 L of this solution for Solution 4.
Add 200 mg of sodium azide to 1 L of ultrapure water.
Stir until the salt is dissolved.
Cool the solution to 4 °C before use.
Prepare a total volume of 260 L of this solution for Solution 5.
Place the pig on the dissection table in the supine position.
Make a midline incision from the xiphoidal process to the pubic bone using a scalpel, exposing all abdominal organs.
Locate and ligate the duodenum orally at the level of the major duodenal papilla using two separate sutures.
Ligate the inferior esophagus with two separate sutures.
Cut between the ligatures with scissors to remove the stomach.
Separate the connective tissue from the colon to reach the small intestine.
Separate the connective tissue of the colon that attaches to the splenic lobe of the pancreas.
Ligate the arteries and remove the colon from the small intestine.
Find the inferior mesenteric vein and artery tree, and ligate them with one suture caudally of the pancreas.
Ligate the splenic artery and vein together with one suture close to the spleen in the hilum.
Cut distally with scissors to remove the spleen.
Follow the duodenum until the duodenal and connection lobes are cleared.
Ligate the duodenum at the end with two separate sutures.
Dissect the portal vein, ligate it with one suture to prevent blood leakage from the liver.
Cut proximally to the ligature on the portal vein.
Find the bile duct and hepatic artery, and ligate them with two sutures.
Cut distally to the sutures for the bile duct and hepatic artery.
Find the aorta under the renal vein and dissect it in the cranial direction from muscle and connective tissue until it reaches the pancreatic area.
Flip the pancreas gently over and dissect the aorta, keeping the SMA and CT intact.
Cut the aorta superior to CT and inferior to SMA with scissors.
Cut the remaining surrounding tissues with scissors and take the pancreas out.
Flush the organ through the aorta with Solution 2 until it perfuses the whole organ or until the whole organ becomes cold.
Keep the pancreas at 4°C or on ice throughout the process.
Cut the sutures of the duodenum using scissors.
Clean the duodenum by flushing 50 - 150 mL of ultrapure water using a 25-mL pipette.
Ligate the cleaned duodenum again with sutures.
Ligate one end of the aorta and all branches besides the SMA and CT with sutures to prevent leakage.
Insert a 4-mm arteriotomy cannula from the other end of the aorta and ligate it with sutures.
Perfuse the pancreas with Solution 3 for 1 hour at 20 mL/min using the decellularization set-up.
Prefill the tubes of pump with solution 3 to ensure no bubbles enter the pancreas.
Ligate all open vascular branches with sutures, except the portal vein.
Freeze the pancreas at -20°C in Solution 4 until the start of the decellularization.
Thaw the pancreas at 4°C.
Run the peristaltic pump in the decellularization set-up with Solution 3 at 20 mL/min until no air bubbles are seen in the detergent inlet tube.
Place the pancreas in the decellularization container and connect the detergent inlet tube to the aorta of the pancreas.
Wash the organ by perfusion with Solution 3 overnight at 20 mL/min at 4°C.
Replace Solution 3 with Solution 5 and perfuse the pancreas for 30 min at 20 mL/min at 4 °C.
Pour out the solution in the organ chamber.
Add Solution 6 and perfuse the pancreas for 8 h at 20 mL/min at 4 °C.
Pour out the solution in the organ chamber.
Wash the organ by perfusion with Solution 5 for 96 h at 20 mL/min at 4 °C.
Pour out the solution in the organ chamber.
Recirculate 500 mL of Dulbecco's PBS containing CaCl2 and MgCl2 for 30 min at 37 °C.
Pour out the solution in the organ chamber.
Add 250 mL of Solution 7 and perfuse the pancreas for 4 h at 20 mL/min at 37 °C.
Pour out the solution in the organ chamber.
Wash the organ by perfusion with Solution 5 for 120 h at 20 mL/min at 4 °C.
Store the organ in Solution 8 at 4 °C for short periods or at -20 °C for long periods.
Cut 3- to 10-mm biopsies from all lobes of the pancreas and fix them in formaldehyde for 48 h at room temperature.
Wash the pieces in ultrapure water for 15 min.
Process the samples in a tissue processor following standard protocols.
Embed the processed samples in paraffin.
Cut 5-µm sections using microtome.
Stain the sections by Meyer's hematoxylin and 0.2% alcoholic eosin (HE) following standard protocols.
View the slides under a light microscope to check for the loss of nuclei.
Use a fresh tissue processed in the same way as a control for checking the presence of nuclei.
